implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player vertical paddles controlled by up/down keys
implemented_requirements.evidence: paddle.py defines Paddle.update reading keys[self.up_key] and keys[self.down_key]; Game.__init__ creates player1 with PLAYER1_KEYS (W/S) and player2 with PLAYER2_KEYS (UP/DOWN).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces off top and bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.check_wall_collisions detects rect.top <= 0 or rect.bottom >= settings.HEIGHT and calls Ball.bounce_top_bottom() which reverses speed_y.

Game.check_paddle_collisions calls Ball.bounce_paddle(paddle) when colliding and moving toward the paddle; bounce_paddle reverses horizontal speed, nudges ball out, speeds up, and angles based on hit offset.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players score a point when opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.check_scoring detects ball.rect.right <= 0 (player 2 missed) or ball.rect.left >= WIDTH (player 1 missed) and calls score_point which updates Scoreboard.
settings.WINNING_SCORE = 5; Scoreboard.has_winner() returns true when a player's score >= winning_score; Game transitions to GAME_OVER when has_winner() is true.
Game.score_point calls self.ball.reset() after updating the score and before entering SERVING state.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game loop with rendering and state handling
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.run() contains the main loop calling handle_events, update, and render each frame; render draws paddles, ball (except during GAME_OVER), scoreboard, and messages.

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete two‑player Pong game. Paddles are controllable via distinct key bindings, the ball correctly bounces off paddles and the top/bottom walls, scoring occurs when the ball exits a side, a configurable winning score ends the match, and the ball is reset after each point with a serve delay. All core mechanics are present and the code appears syntactically correct and ready to run with pygame, so the submission meets the benchmark requirements.
